label: refund_or_compensation
definition: Customer claims money back: refund of fare/fees/taxes, EU261/EC261 delay-cancellation compensation, Avios or points credit, or reimbursement of incurred expenses.
primary_signal: Money or points owed by BA to the customer, or compensation for an incurred/foreseeable loss.
deciding_rule: Any claim that BA owes the customer money or compensation, including via a form or Customer Relations, is this label. Pure policy questions (what is BA allowed to do) are information_or_policy unless the customer frames it as their own claim.

label: booking_change_or_cancellation
definition: Customer asks to modify, add-to, or cancel their own booking: rebooking, adding/removing passengers, changing a date/fare, adding an Avios number or Executive Club detail to an existing PNR, amending names/passports, or cancelling.
primary_signal: A change to an existing booking, not a factual/policy question.
deciding_rule: Data amendments to a PNR (name, passport, Avios add) are this label even when phrased as questions. Problem with the book-a-flight website/App is website_or_app_issue. Cancellation caused by BA alone belongs to refund_or_compensation or flight_disruption.

label: flight_disruption
definition: Customer reports a concrete disruption to their travel: delay, cancellation, diversion, long tarmac wait, misconnect, stranded/reroute, crew/aircraft problems.
primary_signal: A specific, contemporaneous travel event is broken; not a general policy or refund question.
deciding_rule: If the customer leads with a disruption and also asks for money, label disruption and note refund as secondary (disruption caused, claim follows). Delays/cancellations that BA caused but the customer only raises a compensation claim for are refund_or_compensation.

label: baggage
definition: Customer reports a baggage problem: delayed, damaged, lost, misrouted bag, or a carry/checked-item issue (drone, skateboard, laptop, musical instrument on board) with a specific journey.
primary_signal: Bag or carry-on item tied to a real trip.
deciding_rule: Carry-on content disapproval (e.g., robot/drone on board) is this label when the customer wants an answer about their item. Pure policy question about cabin baggage rules is information_or_policy. Fruits/dried-food carry items flagged ambiguous.

label: seat_or_upgrade
definition: Customer asks about or wants seat selection, seat fees, upgrades, or cabin class on a specific booking.
primary_signal: Seats or cabin on their trip.
deciding_rule: Cost claims tied to paid seats/upgrades were labelled seat_or_upgrade only when cheap upgrades are a flight-operational issue rather than seat policy; seat refund disputes with threats may be seat_or_upgrade + secondary contact.

label: website_or_app_issue
definition: Customer reports a technical failure of a BA digital channel: check-in online, Manage My Booking, website errors, app login, payment step, seat selection screen.
primary_signal: Technical failure of the web/App, or enquiry caused by one.
deciding_rule: Login and one-time code problems that trace to web/App are this label; Executive Club account hacking/security is account_or_security. EC number not recognized linked to the site can be website_or_app_issue or account_or_security by trace.

label: account_or_security
definition: Customer reports an Executive Club account or security problem: hacked account, suspect activity, lockout, or identity checks blocking access.
primary_signal: Digital identity/account compromise or security gate.
deciding_rule: Hacked-account claims route to the Executive Club security team (structural escalation) regardless of which channel reported it.

label: contact_or_human_escalation_request
definition: Customer wants meaningful human contact: real contact numbers, human agents, complaint handling, or signals a need for human judgement (heated complaints, threats, legal/regulatory risks, venting with emotional load).
primary_signal: Request for contact channels, a human, or a route needing human judgement.
deciding_rule: Not a money claim (refund_or_compensation) and not an account security case (account_or_security) - this is the remainder: complaints that need a person, phone/web numbers, review submission, legal/regulatory pressure. Ambiguous vents flagged unclear_intent.

label: information_or_policy
definition: Customer asks a factual question about BA policy, quick service facts (check-in times, arrival time), eligibility rules, or product facts that do not need a booking change.
primary_signal: A standalone knowable fact or policy question.
deciding_rule: An answer fully satisfies the query (AUTO_HANDLE). If answering requires account-gated data the resolution is still an off-thread hand-off, but the intent stays information.

label: noise_or_off_topic_or_ack
definition: Non-service traffic: praise, thanks, banter, sarcastic venting with no actionable request, marketing interactions, off-topic commentary, or a plain acknowledgement.
deciding_rule: Sarcastic 'thanks for cancelling the program' with no request is noise. Complaints with a real unresolved issue are contact_or_human_escalation_request, not noise, even if short.
